headline: High: Continue can feed untrusted workspace content into n8n workflows, creating default-path prompt-injection and data-leak risks with shared filesystem and broad egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue reads workspace files and uses MCP/tool calls, while n8n can ingest workflow inputs and execute downstream actions. Because Continue can surface raw file content and n8n can operationalize it, attacker-controlled text in shared files can become instructions. The pair’s shared filesystem bridge makes this interaction plausible by default.
conditions: IF Continue reads attacker-controlled workspace content and passes it into an n8n workflow input
IF n8n treats that input as instructions or prompt text without provenance checks
mitigations: Restrict Continue to read-only review mode for untrusted files
Add a manual approval step before any n8n workflow consumes AI-generated text
Tag and reject untrusted file-derived content in workflow inputs
Use separate workspaces for assistant output and workflow input
requires-engineering: add provenance tracking between IDE content and n8n nodes

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue can read workspace files and has broad network egress; n8n can read server files and call many integration APIs. If sensitive code or secrets are present in the shared workspace, either agent can move them into external services. The pair therefore creates a default-path exfiltration risk, not just a local-only leak.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared workspace or n8n server filesystem
IF either agent sends file-derived context to an external model or integration API
mitigations: Limit both agents to a sanitized project subset
Disable external integrations for workflows handling secrets
Use separate credentials and workspaces for code and automation
Review outbound destinations before running workflows
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction on file-derived prompts and workflow payloads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue writes workspace files and shares state via filesystem across IDE instances; n8n writes server files and runs commands/subprocesses. Both can mutate overlapping filesystem-backed resources without a locking primitive in the profiles, so concurrent edits or workflow writes can clobber each other. The conflict is default-dangerous because both have write access.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or file-backed artifact
IF n8n workflows or Continue sessions run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories to each agent
Pause one agent while the other writes shared artifacts
Use file locks or a queue around shared outputs
Keep generated artifacts in separate branches or folders
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking for shared filesystem writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can generate code or explanations that n8n may consume as workflow inputs, and n8n can then execute actions through integrations or command nodes. That makes A’s output a potential authority source for B, with no documented verification step between them. Errors can cascade into real actions, so the blast radius exceeds a simple bad suggestion.
conditions: IF n8n uses Continue-generated text to configure or trigger workflow steps
IF no human or rule-based verification occurs before execution
mitigations: Require human review before workflow execution
Constrain n8n to read-only dry runs for AI-generated inputs
Validate generated commands against an allowlist
Separate drafting from execution workflows
requires-engineering: add schema validation for AI-produced workflow payloads

E_compliance.rationale: Continue handles editor buffers and workspace files, while n8n processes whatever the workflow touches and stores credentials on its server. If regulated data such as EU PII or secrets enters both systems, their differing storage and integration surfaces can create retention or residency mismatches. The profiles do not prove a specific legal violation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed in the shared workspace or n8n workflows
IF retention, residency, or logging settings differ between the IDE and n8n server
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through both agents
Minimize logging on workflows that touch sensitive data
Set short retention on n8n execution history
Store secrets only in dedicated credential stores
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for both systems
